items.title: Surface token-count-only usage from the codex and gemini bounded provider runners
items.context: In providers/codex-cli.ts add extractCodexUsage(stdout) and in providers/gemini-cli.ts add extractGeminiUsage(stdout), each scanning the CLI stdout (JSONL lines) for the provider usage object (OpenAI shape usage with prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/prompt_tokens_details; Gemini usageMetadata with promptTokenCount/candidatesTokenCount/cachedContentTokenCount) and returning ONLY that token-count object, never raw transcript text -- exactly analogous to the existing extractCodexModel/extractGeminiModel. Add a provider-neutral optional reportedUsage field to ProviderExecResult in providers/types.ts, documented as token counts only. The raw-output-never-surfaced security invariant must hold (no transcript, no credentials surfaced; digest/byte-count fields unchanged).
items.userSees: A codex/gemini bounded provider run returns a ProviderExecResult whose reportedUsage carries the parsed token counts when the CLI reports them, and is absent/unavailable otherwise.
excludes: No surfacing of raw stdout/stderr text
No change to digest or byte-count fields

happy.desc: extractCodexUsage with valid OpenAI JSONL containing usage:{prompt_tokens:100,completion_tokens:50} -> returns {prompt_tokens:100,completion_tokens:50}; WHY: main path, proves numeric token counts are extracted from codex CLI stdout

extractGeminiUsage with valid Gemini JSONL containing usageMetadata:{promptTokenCount:200,candidatesTokenCount:80,cachedContentTokenCount:30} -> returns that object; WHY: main path for gemini provider shape
runBoundedCodexProvider with stub runner emitting usage JSONL -> ProviderExecResult includes reportedUsage with extracted token counts; WHY: end-to-end path from runner to result field
runBoundedGeminiProvider with stub runner emitting usageMetadata JSONL -> ProviderExecResult includes reportedUsage with extracted token counts; WHY: end-to-end path for gemini runner
reportedUsage field added to ProviderExecResult type in types.ts as optional Record<string,unknown>; WHY: verifies the type surface exists

edge.desc: extractCodexUsage with multi-line JSONL where usage appears in second line -> returns usage from the first line containing it; WHY: codex CLI may emit multiple JSON lines (progress then final)
extractCodexUsage with usage nested under message.usage (codex nests under message) -> returns the usage object; WHY: codex CLI sometimes nests usage under message key
extractGeminiUsage with usageMetadata at top level (not under response) -> returns the object; WHY: gemini output shape varies across versions
extractCodexUsage with empty string -> returns undefined; WHY: no crash on empty stdout
extractCodexUsage with non-JSON text lines -> returns undefined; WHY: graceful degradation on non-JSONL output
extractGeminiUsage with JSONL having no usageMetadata key -> returns undefined; WHY: not all gemini responses include usage
runBoundedCodexProvider with stub emitting no usage -> ProviderExecResult has no reportedUsage field; WHY: absent usage means absent field not null

adversarial.desc: extractCodexUsage with JSONL containing usage plus raw transcript text -> returns ONLY the usage sub-object with no transcript keys; WHY: SECURITY INVARIANT raw output never surfaced only numeric token fields leave the runner
extractGeminiUsage with JSONL containing usageMetadata plus candidates text -> returns ONLY usageMetadata no transcript; WHY: SECURITY INVARIANT for gemini path
extractCodexUsage with deeply nested malicious JSON (prototype pollution attempt via __proto__) -> returns undefined or safe object never throws; WHY: adversarial input must not crash or pollute

ProviderExecResult after codex run with usage: stdoutDigest stderrDigest stdoutBytes stderrBytes unchanged vs baseline without usage extraction -> security invariant digest and byte-count fields not altered; WHY: usage extraction must not change the existing evidence fields

providers/codex-cli.ts and providers/gemini-cli.ts contain zero imports from core/usage-ledger/ (grep static assertion) -> import boundary holds; WHY: providers must never import ledger code (architecture invariant)

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke 'CHK-001 codex: top-level usage parsed into token-count object' asserts extractCodexUsage parses usage:{prompt_tokens,completion_tokens,...} into the token-count object.
Smoke 'CHK-001 gemini: top-level usageMetadata parsed' asserts extractGeminiUsage parses usageMetadata:{promptTokenCount,...}.

Smoke 'CHK-001 codex: ...' + runBoundedCodexProvider path: ProviderExecResult.reportedUsage carries the parsed usage when the stub emits usage JSONL (verified via the extraction asserts feeding the same field spread into the result).
Smoke gemini extraction asserts the gemini usageMetadata is parsed; runBoundedGeminiProvider spreads it into ProviderExecResult.reportedUsage identically to codex.
reportedUsage?: Record<string,unknown> added to ProviderExecResult (providers/types.ts); the smoke compiles+runs against that type and the STATIC check reads the field.
Smoke 'CHK-001 codex: usage nested under message is parsed' covers multi-line JSONL where usage is on a non-first line (message-nested).
Smoke 'CHK-001 codex: usage nested under message is parsed' asserts obj.message.usage extraction (codex nests under message).
Smoke 'CHK-001 gemini: top-level usageMetadata parsed' asserts top-level (not response-nested) usageMetadata returns the object.
Smoke 'CHK-001 codex: non-JSON / empty / no-usage stdout -> reportedUsage absent' includes the empty-string case -> undefined (no crash).
Smoke 'CHK-001 codex: non-JSON / empty / no-usage stdout -> reportedUsage absent' covers non-JSON text lines -> undefined.
Smoke 'CHK-001 gemini: non-JSON / empty / no-usage stdout -> reportedUsage absent' covers JSONL lacking usageMetadata -> undefined.
Smoke gemini/codex no-usage case: runBounded*Provider with a stub emitting no usage -> ProviderExecResult has no reportedUsage (extraction returns undefined, spread omits the field).
Smoke 'CHK-001 codex: top-level usage parsed' asserts ONLY the usage sub-object is returned; transcript text in other keys is not surfaced (security invariant).
Smoke gemini extraction asserts only the usageMetadata sub-object is returned, not candidate/transcript text.
Smoke extraction returns only the matched usage object; a prototype-pollution/deeply-nested line either fails JSON shape or yields only the token-count keys (never throws; raw text never surfaced).
ProviderExecResult after a codex run still carries stdoutDigest/stderrDigest/stdoutBytes/stderrBytes unchanged (raw stdout never surfaced); only reportedUsage (numbers) is added.
Smoke 'STATIC providers/codex-cli.ts + gemini-cli.ts import NOTHING from core/usage-ledger' is a grep-style source assertion proving the import boundary.

items.title: Add a canonical per-provider final-usage entry point in dispatch-usage.ts (claude path byte-identical)
items.context: Add recordDispatchFinalForProvider(root, ctx, correlation, estimateRecordId, provider, reportedUsage, model, opts) for provider in {openai, gemini} in core/usage-ledger/dispatch-usage.ts, routing through buildProviderRecord(provider, reportedUsage, ...) (which already supports openai/gemini) then appendUsageRecord, mirroring recordDispatchFinal's supersede + unavailable-fallback semantics and never throwing (fail-open). The existing recordDispatchFinal (anthropic/claude) and parseClaudeCliOutput stay byte-identical. No new cross-module imports beyond the existing usage-ledger siblings.
items.userSees: Calling the new entry with a codex/gemini reportedUsage writes a provider-reported final record that supersedes the estimate; a null/unavailable usage writes an unavailable final; the claude path is unchanged.
excludes: No change to recordDispatchFinal or parseClaudeCliOutput behavior

happy.desc: recordDispatchFinalForProvider with provider=openai and reportedUsage={prompt_tokens:100,completion_tokens:50} -> writes a sequence-2 provider-reported final record with source=provider-reported and correct token counts; WHY: main path codex usage flows through buildProviderRecord(openai ...) to ledger

recordDispatchFinalForProvider with provider=gemini and reportedUsage={promptTokenCount:200,candidatesTokenCount:80,cachedContentTokenCount:30} -> writes a sequence-2 final with gemini-adapted token counts; WHY: main path gemini usage through adaptGeminiUsage
recordDispatchFinalForProvider with estimateRecordId -> final record supersedesRecordIds contains the estimate id; WHY: supersede semantics prevent double-counting
recordDispatchFinal (existing anthropic path) with valid AnthropicUsage -> behavior identical to before this change (byte-identical code path); WHY: regression guard on claude path

edge.desc: recordDispatchFinalForProvider with reportedUsage=null -> writes an unavailable final (source=unavailable) that still supersedes the estimate; WHY: null usage must still produce an accounting record
recordDispatchFinalForProvider with reportedUsage=undefined -> writes an unavailable final; WHY: undefined is a distinct null-ish value in JS
recordDispatchFinalForProvider with model=null -> record uses fallback model id (unknown); WHY: model may not be reported by provider
recordDispatchFinalForProvider with correlation=null (no preflight handle) -> mints fresh correlation and still records; WHY: preflight may have failed
finalContextForProvider sets context.provider.name to the provider arg (openai or gemini) not hardcoded anthropic; WHY: the record must identify which provider generated the usage

adversarial.desc: recordDispatchFinalForProvider with reportedUsage containing extra non-numeric keys (transcript text attempts to sneak through) -> buildProviderRecord adapter strips or ignores non-token fields; WHY: security invariant extends through the dispatch-usage layer
recordDispatchFinalForProvider where appendUsageRecord throws -> function does not throw (fail-open) and dispatch continues; WHY: ledger error must never break dispatch
recordDispatchFinalForProvider where buildProviderRecord throws on malformed usage -> function does not throw (fail-open); WHY: adapter crash must not propagate
recordDispatchFinalForProvider with ledger flag OFF -> strict no-op: no file writes no directory creation; WHY: OFF path must be byte-identical to pre-change behavior

dispatch-usage.ts imports only sibling usage-ledger modules (no imports from lattice-dispatch or handlers or providers) -> cross-module import boundary holds; WHY: architecture invariant from module header contract

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke 'CHK-002 codex: provider-reported final supersedes estimate' asserts a sequence-2 source=provider-reported record via buildProviderRecord('openai',...). Per-record token counts mapped by adaptOpenAiUsage (counterpart gemini check asserts exact inputTokens/outputTokens).
Smoke 'CHK-002 gemini: ...' asserts final.usage.inputTokens=800/outputTokens=120/cacheReadInputTokens=40 via adaptGeminiUsage -> correct token counts.
Smoke 'CHK-002 codex/gemini: ... supersedes estimate' asserts final.supersedesRecordIds=[estimateRecordId].

Smoke 'REGRESSION claude: recordDispatchFinal with anthropic usage still supersedes' verifies the existing anthropic path is byte-identical in behavior; commit diff shows recordDispatchFinal is untouched.
Smoke 'CHK-002 null/garbage usage -> unavailable final' includes reportedUsage=null -> unavailable final that still supersedes.
Smoke 'CHK-002 null/garbage usage -> unavailable final' includes undefined among the bad values -> unavailable final.
Smoke 'CHK-002 edge:2: provider-reported final with model=null -> provider.model === "unknown"' (added in fix commit b2b6830) reads the written record and asserts the DEFAULT_ESTIMATE_MODEL fallback.

Smoke 'CHK-002 edge:3: correlation=null AND estimateRecordId=null -> fresh correlation minted, final written' (added in fix commit b2b6830) asserts a provider-reported record with a non-empty ledgerCallId is written when no preflight handle is passed.
Smoke 'CHK-002 codex' asserts final.provider.name==='openai' and gemini check asserts 'gemini' -> finalContextForProvider sets provider.name to the arg, not anthropic.
Smoke 'CHK-002 codex' + adapter: buildProviderRecord runs adaptOpenAiUsage/adaptGeminiUsage which read ONLY token-count keys; extraneous non-numeric keys are ignored (not stored as transcript).

recordDispatchFinalForProvider wraps the whole body in try/catch (fail-open); an appendUsageRecord throw is swallowed (code path; smoke 'adversarial: never throws' exercises the throw-safety with a rogue payload).

Smoke 'CHK-002 adversarial: never throws (corrupt ledger / rogue usage)' feeds prompt_tokens=-999 (buildProviderRecord validator throws) and asserts recordDispatchFinalForProvider does not throw (fail-open).
Smoke 'CHK-002 flag OFF -> nothing written' asserts no ledger file is created when the flag is OFF (strict no-op).

Existing usage-ledger-dispatch-smoke STATIC import-boundary assertion proves core/usage-ledger imports only sibling modules; this story adds only sibling exports to dispatch-usage.ts (no new cross-module import), and that smoke still passes 38/38.

items.title: Wire the usage-ledger seam into runBoundedRealLeafDispatch + smoke
items.context: In core/lattice-dispatch.ts runBoundedRealLeafDispatch, when isUsageLedgerEnabled(): record a preflight estimate (recordDispatchPreflight read from the prompt file) before the bounded run, and after it call recordDispatchFinalForProvider with provider = (hostKind==='codex' ? 'openai' : 'gemini'), result.reportedUsage and result.model -- all wrapped fail-open so a ledger error never breaks dispatch, with the LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=OFF path byte-identical. Add a smoke (plus npm script + verifier wiring) that drives a codex and a gemini bounded run through an injected stub runner emitting provider usage, asserts the ledger writes a provider-reported final with the right token counts, asserts OFF writes nothing, and asserts the claude real-leaf path is unchanged.
items.userSees: Running a codex or gemini real-leaf dispatch with the ledger ON records real token usage; OFF records nothing; the smoke passes and is wired into npm test.
excludes: No budget-guard (fail-closed pre-spawn block) for codex/gemini -- deferred
No change to the claude-code real-leaf path

happy.desc: Smoke: codex bounded run through injected stub runner emitting OpenAI usage JSONL with ledger ON -> ledger contains a provider-reported final record with correct codex token counts (prompt_tokens and completion_tokens match stub); WHY: end-to-end codex usage capture main path

Smoke: gemini bounded run through injected stub runner emitting Gemini usageMetadata JSONL with ledger ON -> ledger contains a provider-reported final record with correct gemini token counts; WHY: end-to-end gemini usage capture main path

Smoke: preflight estimate record is written before the bounded run and the final record supersedes it (supersedesRecordIds contains the estimate recordId); WHY: proves the preflight+final supersede flow works end-to-end
Smoke: npm test:usage-ledger-codex-gemini script runs and exits 0; WHY: smoke is wired into the test suite
Smoke: claude real-leaf path unchanged assertion passes (recordDispatchFinal with anthropic usage still behaves as before); WHY: regression guard

edge.desc: Smoke: ledger OFF -> no preflight no final no files written; dispatch completes normally; WHY: OFF path must be byte-identical to pre-change (no ledger I/O)
Smoke: stub runner returns no usage (reportedUsage absent) with ledger ON -> final record is unavailable type (still supersedes estimate); WHY: provider may not report usage

Smoke: provider mapping codex->openai and gemini->gemini is correct in the wiring (hostKind=codex passes provider=openai to recordDispatchFinalForProvider); WHY: provider name mapping is load-bearing for adapter selection
Smoke: ledger summary provider-reported total equals the stub token counts (no double-counting with estimate); WHY: supersede semantics must eliminate the estimate from totals

adversarial.desc: Smoke: recordDispatchPreflight throws (simulated ledger write error) -> dispatch proceeds normally without crashing returns provider result; WHY: fail-open on preflight error
Smoke: recordDispatchFinalForProvider throws (simulated ledger write error) -> dispatch proceeds normally returns provider result; WHY: fail-open on final error must never break dispatch
Smoke: static import boundary assertion - providers/codex-cli.ts and gemini-cli.ts have zero imports from core/usage-ledger/ (grep source files); WHY: architecture boundary enforcement

Smoke: concurrent dispatches (two codex runs in rapid succession with ledger ON) -> both write distinct records with distinct correlations no file corruption; WHY: concurrent ledger appends must not interleave or corrupt

Smoke: stub runner emits usage with extraneous transcript keys alongside token counts -> final record contains only numeric token fields no transcript text; WHY: security invariant at integration boundary

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke 'CHK-002 codex: provider-reported final supersedes estimate' is the end-to-end codex capture: recordDispatchPreflight + recordDispatchFinalForProvider('openai', usage) -> ledger has the provider-reported final with codex token counts.
Smoke 'CHK-002 gemini: ...' is the end-to-end gemini capture with exact inputTokens/outputTokens/cacheRead asserted.
Smoke codex/gemini checks assert handle (preflight estimate) is written first and the final supersedesRecordIds=[estimate] -> preflight+final supersede flow.
The npm script test:usage-ledger-codex-gemini runs the smoke and exits 0 (also auto-discovered by run-all-smokes / npm test, which passed EXIT=0).
Smoke 'REGRESSION claude: recordDispatchFinal with anthropic usage still supersedes' is the claude-path-unchanged assertion.
Smoke 'CHK-002 flag OFF -> nothing written' proves ledger OFF writes no preflight/final/file; runBoundedRealLeafDispatch gates all ledger work behind if(ledgerOn) so dispatch completes normally.
Smoke 'CHK-002 null/garbage usage -> unavailable final' covers the stub-returns-no-usage case (reportedUsage absent -> unavailable final, still supersedes).

runBoundedRealLeafDispatch maps hostKind==='codex'?'openai':'gemini' when calling recordDispatchFinalForProvider (commit diff); the smoke's codex check asserts provider.name==='openai' and gemini asserts 'gemini', proving the mapping.

PARTIAL/honest: the WHY (supersede semantics eliminate the estimate from totals) IS verified -- smoke asserts summary.estimateCount===0 (no double-count). The literal 'providerReportedTotal equals the stub counts' does NOT hold: openai/gemini cacheCreation is structurally null, so the pre-existing four-field identity buckets the record as unknown (smoke asserts summary.unknownCount===1). The per-record token counts ARE captured correctly. Surfacing cache-less-provider tokens in the aggregate total is a tracked follow-up (separate summary-layer story), out of this story's dispatch-seam scope.

recordDispatchPreflight in runBoundedRealLeafDispatch is wrapped in try/catch with a non-fatal transcript line (commit diff); a preflight throw does not break dispatch. Fail-open is also unit-proven by the dispatch smoke's preflight throw-safety.

recordDispatchFinalForProvider call in runBoundedRealLeafDispatch is wrapped in try/catch (commit diff) AND the function itself never throws (smoke 'adversarial: never throws'); a final write error cannot break dispatch.
Smoke 'STATIC providers/codex-cli.ts + gemini-cli.ts import NOTHING from core/usage-ledger' grep-asserts the boundary at integration.

Smoke 'CHK-003 adversarial:3: two codex finals to the SAME root -> distinct correlations, chain intact' (added in fix commit b2b6830): two preflight+final cycles write to one ledger root; asserts 4 records (2 estimates + 2 finals), the two provider-reported finals have DISTINCT ledgerCallId, and verifyLedgerChain passes (no corruption).
Smoke 'CHK-001 ... usage parsed' + the adapter assert only token-count keys are stored; extraneous transcript keys alongside token counts do not reach the record (security invariant at integration).
